newsitem.title: UK: Excerpts from speech by UK Labour's Blair.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from speech by UK Labour's Blair.

text.p: Following is a summary of British opposition Labour leader Tony Blair's remarks on economic policy in his speech to the party conference:

- Blair described Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke as his secret weapon -- "Mr Feelgood factor.' "I'll tell you when the real feelgood factor will arrive: when people say goodbye to this government for good."
- The true radical mission of the Labour party was not to hold people back but to help them get on.

- "Today we compete in the era of global markets. There is no future for Britain as a low wage, low skills, low tech economy. We compete on quality or not at all. This means a stable economy, long-term investment and the enterprise of the people set free."

- "Labour will be the party of sound finance and good housekeeping. World interest rates and inflation rates low. In Britain, under Labour, we will keep them this way. These will be defined targets, set and kept to. Losing control of public finances isn't radical, it's just reckless."

"We need a tax regime that is fair and encourages work and business. Sure, the few at the top have become wealthy under the Tories, but they have put up the taxes of ordinary families in Britain by the largest amount in peacetime history. We are not trying to add to their burden. Instead, a new Labour government should try to get tax down for low income earners, some of them paying 80 or 90 percent marginal tax rates."

"Labour is the party of small business in Britain today. We will give Britain a modern integrated transport network, built in partnership between public and private finance and restoring a unified system of railways with a publicly owned, publicly accountable BR at its core."

- Blair said he would build a new constructive relationship with Britain's EU partners and would not scrap Britain's veto. Options on a single currency would remain open. Noting that Britain would hold the EU presidency in the first half of 1998, he set a deadline of June 1998 for completing the single market.
- The Labour leader pledged a statutory national minimum wage and said Britain would join the EU's social chapter.

- On industrial relations, he said there would be "fairness, not favours for employers and employees alike. The Labour government is not the political arm of anyone today other than the British people."
- Blair said his three main priorities were "education, education and education."

- "Today, I offer you, and we offer the country, a new vision. If we are to build this new age of achievement, you and I, and all of us together, must first build the decent society to deliver it. A society in which every individual is valued, every person given a chance to develop their potential, a society to which we contribute and which contributes to us."

- As a first step, Blair said Labour would implement a programme to take 250,000 young people off benefit and into work, financed by a windfall levy on the profits of privatised utilities. It would release money from the sale of council houses to finance home-building.

- On pensions, he said a Labour government would do its duty by British pensioners and a review would be carried out. "But I will not make promises on money until I know that they can be kept. This is our guiding rule and there can be no exceptions to it. I ask you to understand that."
- Blair said Labour would scrap the internal market in the National Health Service and improve the NHS as a decent public service.

- Blair outlined a "performance contract" on which he said a Labour government should be judged. It includes a pledge that by the end of its five-year term, the government would have increased the proportion of national income spent on education, on "the welfare bills of social failure," cut the number of long-term unemployed and cut by over a half the number of young people unemployed, kept government borrowing low and "inflation within the low and prudent targets we set within the economic cycle."
- Labour was a democratic socialist party but it stood in a tradition "bigger than European Social Democracy, bigger than any -ism."

- "Labour's coming home and the people are coming home because Britain is their team and they're part of it. And they know that if we unleash the potential of our people, Britain comes alive with the new energy, the new ideas and the new leadership and Britain can take on the world and win."
